method: After freezing and replaying the pair, returned to the adopted 2026–27 faculty PDF and separately rebuilt the three 60 EC years from Appendices 3.1 and 3.2. Rechecked Appendix 12.3 against the regular table, and the thesis conditions against its individual catalog entry. Reconsidered the organizing questions, course contributions and academic limits of the three UCR plans from the current workbook. This was a separate same-AI pass.
findings: The mainly Dutch-taught Business Administration BSc has a 60 EC common first year and three profiles. Business and Management is the least specialized general management profile and illustrates the generic degree. Appendix 3.1 confirms twelve 5 EC courses. Academic Skills, Business Consulting and Microeconomics appear in the current year-one table. Appendix 3.2 confirms twelve 5 EC second-year courses in management, accounting, finance, operations, organization and research. Year three includes 30 EC of eligible minor or exchange, a 10 EC thesis and four 5 EC courses, including Entrepreneurship Lab. Appendix 12.3 permits earlier Academic Skills I and II and the Integrative Research Project as transition substitutions for students who completed them. Those historic names are excluded from the regular curriculum illustrated here.

The official first-year table progresses from management and academic foundations to statistics, management accounting and microeconomics. The second-year specialization develops organizational theory and qualitative methods, then quantitative methods, operations, research design, market research and strategy. The current thesis catalog requires 60 EC in first-year study and 60 EC of compulsory profile-specific study, as well as degree-program approval before the thesis. The 30 EC choice remains explicit. No particular minor or exchange destination is assumed.

The broad plan connects business foundations, product design, marketing and strategy to workplace behavior, governance, business law, and quantitative and qualitative research. The technology plan builds programming, databases, data science, algorithms and machine learning, with statistics and mathematical methods supporting analysis and AI ethics and strategy connecting methods to business. Computer science methods are applied tools, not an operations engineering sequence. The finance plan develops accounting, economics, finance, probability, econometrics and behavioral economics with applied research. Transnational business law gives commercial and trade context without standing in for auditing or control. The three schedules differ materially in the weight of management and people, computing and business systems, or finance and decision evidence. The reviewed matches cover shared accounting, organization, marketing, microeconomics, methods and digital transformation. Dedicated supply chains, consulting, operations, management control and the required thesis are distinguished from UCR contributions.
